subject: International processing assurances & SIEM log schema
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@soteriahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@soteriahealth.com
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: international processing assurances and log format

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough. Our security and platform teams need a few clarifications to complete the RFP: primarily around whether Redwood will act as processor for EU personal data in the pilot, how you document transfer safeguards in the contract, and a sample of the per-tenant audit log for SIEM ingestion. Specific asks: 

1) Confirm processor/controller stance for the pilot (we will send pseudonymized patient identifiers).
2) Provide the DPA annex or an annex excerpt that points to the transfer safeguards and retention rules for transient caches.
3) Share a redacted sample of the tenant-level audit log (CSV) and a short ingestion README — our SIEM needs field names/types.

Can you respond by Thu EOD so procurement can proceed? Happy to schedule a 30-minute call if easier.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of Security Operations
Soteria Health

[Attachment: Soteria_RFP_Log_Requests.docx]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international processing assurances and log format

Hi Elena 

Appreciate the clear list. High level: Redwood will operate as a processor for customer-supplied personal data in hosted and dedicated modes; controller-to-controller transfers are possible only when customers explicitly configure data egress to their own infrastructure (we will document that in the annex).

Plan:
- Marissa will attach an annex excerpt mapping transfer safeguards and retention.
- Karthik will supply a redacted log sample + ingest README.
- I'll propose a short tech-review with your SIEM engineer to validate fields.

I'll aim to get the attachments to you by Wednesday.

Rachel
Senior Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international processing assurances and log format

Rachel/Karthik,

Attached is an annex excerpt (redwood_processing_annex_v2.pdf) that we can provide as a starter redline. Highlights included:
- Section 2: Parties/roles and a fill-in for controller/processor depending on data types.
- Section 3: Transfers & Safeguards: describes logical KMS separation, fallback routing behavior, and a default cache TTL.
- Section 5: Retention: default log retention and options for Dedicated/Private customers.

I've left two placeholders where Soteria legal should indicate whether patient identifiers will be considered pseudonymized prior to upload.

Marissa
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international processing assurances and log format

Team,

I've prepared a redacted audit log sample and an ingestion README (attached). Key implementation notes for the RFI response: 

- Log fields exported: timestamp (ISO8601), tenant_id, request_id, user_principal (hashed if needed), action, endpoint, resource_id, src_ip (anonymized on request), outcome, bytes_sent.
- Encryption & keys: hosted mode uses tenant-scoped keys (logical separation). BYOK supported: we never hold plaintext. Dedicated/Private supports HSM-backed keys.
- Caching: ephemeral serving-tier caches are encrypted and have configurable TTL; default for cross-border fallback is 15 minutes, can be zero for pilot.
- Export: logs can be streamed to customer S3/GCS or provided via secure download for SIEM ingestion.

I've attached log_sample_redacted.csv and ingest_readme_v2.txt.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@soteriahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international processing assurances and log format

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our SIEM and legal: 

- SIEM: the sample looks good but can you provide the header row as JSON Schema as well for automated mapping?
- Legal: please confirm that, in hosted mode with Redwood-managed keys, keys are logically partitioned per tenant and not co-mingled; also we need the exact cache TTL language for the annex redline.

If you can provide the JSON Schema snippet and a sentence for the cache TTL clause today, procurement can issue a term sheet.

Elena
Head of Security Operations
Soteria Health

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@soteriahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: international processing assurances and log format

Elena,

Attached: log_sample_redacted.csv, ingest_readme_v2.txt, and an annex snippet. Quick answers inline: 

- JSON Schema: included in ingest_readme_v2.txt (simple mapping for timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, user_principal_hashed, action, endpoint, resource_id, src_ip_masked, outcome, bytes_sent).
- Key partitioning: hosted Redwood-managed keys are logically partitioned per-tenant within our KMS namespace; tenants do not share key material. BYOK places key material under the customer's control.
- Cache TTL clause (annex language): "In hosted deployments, ephemeral serving caches used for request routing may persist encrypted fragments of request data for a default maximum of 15 minutes; Customer may request TTL=0 for pilot or production enforcement where regional replicas exist."

Next steps: Marissa will produce a redline for Soteria legal and I will schedule a 30-minute ingestion review with your SIEM engineer (please share an invite).

Rachel
Senior Manager, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood_processing_annex_v2.pdf, log_sample_redacted.csv, ingest_readme_v2.txt]
